interest: Documents how Japanese merchant marine training directly informed the creation of the U.S. Maritime Service.
keywords: Bureau of Marine Inspection and Navigation
overview: This file centers on an extensive August 1938 voluntary consular report by American Vice Consul Beppo R. Johansen in Yokohama detailing the training of personnel for the Japanese merchant marine. The report comprehensively examines Japan's nautical education system, legal framework, government colleges, prefectural schools, curricula, and practical training on sailing ships and in shipyards. The remainder of the file consists of State Department transmittal memoranda distributing the report to the U.S. Coast Guard, the Bureau of Marine Inspection and Navigation, and the U.S. Maritime Commission, all of which praised it as excellent and utilized its insights to assist in organizing the U.S. Maritime Service and developing American seaman training programs. The file concludes with commendatory evaluations forwarded back to Yokohama and a cross-reference note on shipping American seamen at Kobe.
